description: replace caller-supplied active-bracket inputs with the complete official 2026 Missouri eight-bracket schedule

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module claimed to implement the section 143.011 schedule and cited its bracket rows as proof atoms, but encoded none of the statute's eight brackets or their selection conditions: it applied one caller-supplied base/floor/rate linear piece to any taxable income, so for income outside the supplied bracket it returned a figure the statute's table does not produce (e.g. $263 rather than $89.68 on $5,000 of taxable income).
triage.triage_notes: Read the cited provisions through the pinned corpus release: us-mo/statute/143.011 subsection 1 lists exactly the eight rows the fix adds (0/1,348/2,696/4,044/5,392/6,740/8,088/9,436 with bases 0,0,27,61,101,148,202,263 and rates 0,2.0,2.5,3.0,3.5,4.0,4.5,4.7%), so every added parameter value matches the source, and the new bracket selection uses 'ti <= upper[k]', matching the source's 'Over $X but not over $Y' inclusive-upper phrasing. The commit bundles several other changes that each have an independent fidelity flavor and could support a different kind label: entity moves TaxUnit -> Person (143.011 'imposed ... on the Missouri taxable income of every resident' and 143.021 'Every resident having a taxable income shall determine his or her tax' are per-individual, so the old TaxUnit grain was wrong_entity_or_scope); every version gains effective_to '2026-12-31' where the pre-fix versions were open-ended even though 143.011 subsection 5 inflation-adjusts the brackets annually (wrong_period_or_effective_date); and the output rule is renamed from '..._income_tax_liability' to '..._income_tax_before_credits_indiv', dropping an over-claimed 'liability' surface. I chose unrepresented_clause because the PR's lead bullet and the bulk of the diff are about the missing statutory schedule. Counter-argument a reviewer should weigh: the pre-fix module's own rationale openly declared the bracket values 'caller-supplied current-authority inputs' (status composed_from_supplied_current_authority), so this can be read as a pilot being upgraded in scope rather than a targeted defect fix; the commit subject is 'Encode Missouri 2026 individual tax schedule', the commit body is empty, and the PR has zero reviews/comments (its own text says 'Draft only. Independent review-fix cycle is pending and required before readiness.') yet it was merged 2026-07-22. Hence confidence held at 0.6. No follow-up commits touch this file; its only prior commit is 699cc028f which created the pilot. Non-module changes in the commit: oracle-coverage-pending.yaml ledger entries (ceiling 1699 -> 1703, renamed legal_ids) and the signed encoding manifest, both bookkeeping.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix module did not silently omit the eight brackets: its header declared `status: composed_from_supplied_current_authority` and its rationale said it "accepts completed-return Missouri taxable income and the active bracket's cumulative base tax, floor, and marginal rate as caller-supplied current-authority inputs", the same sanctioned pilot pattern the sibling us-dc module uses at the same parent commit, so internalizing the schedule is largely coverage the module expressly declared out of scope (and the reader's $5,000 → $263 example requires a caller to supply a non-active bracket, violating that stated contract). What the diff changes that the source does contradict is grain and output surface: every rule moves from `entity: TaxUnit` to `entity: Person` and the output is renamed from `mo_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` to `mo_pit_pilot_income_tax_before_credits_indiv`, while the pinned corpus text of Mo. Rev. Stat. 143.011 imposes the tax "on the Missouri taxable income of every resident" and 143.021 says "Every resident having a taxable income shall determine his or her tax from the rates provided in section 143.011". Applying a per-resident graduated schedule to a TaxUnit aggregate mis-states the tax for any multi-earner unit (the pre-fix grid used only one-earner joint cases, which masked it; the fix adds `dual_person_y_companion_9100` / `dual_person_s_companion_3900`), and "liability" over-claimed an output that excludes credits. So it is a fidelity defect, but wrong_entity_or_scope is the kind that survives the module's own scope disclaimer.
triage.verifier_quote:
-  - name: mo_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability
+  - name: mo_pit_pilot_income_tax_before_credits_indiv
     kind: derived
-    entity: TaxUnit
+    entity: Person
triage.verifier_notes:
Both kinds are genuinely present in this one commit; the reviewer should decide which the corpus item is meant to capture.

Case for keeping the first reader's unrepresented_clause (the strongest counter to my reclassify): the pinned corpus record for us-mo/statute/143.011 (release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, body sha d6a5131…) contains all eight rows verbatim ("$0 to $1,348: $0" … "Over $9,436: $263 plus 4.7% of excess over $9,436"), and the pre-fix rule `mo_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` cited four of those rows as `kind: formula` proof atoms on `versions[0].formula` under `proof_validation: required: true`, while that formula was only `mo_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_base + mo_pit_pilot_supplied_marginal_rate * max(0, mo_pit_pilot_taxable_income - mo_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_floor)` — i.e. it asserted formula-level evidence from bracket rows it did not encode, and 143.021.2(1)'s zero-tax band was likewise unrepresented. If the reviewer holds that formula proof atoms citing a row constitute a claim to implement that row, unrepresented_clause stands and the verdict should be confirmed.

Case against: the disclaimer is explicit and repo-wide, not an oversight. us-dc/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml at the parent commit e9b82eac uses the identical status and says "All tax-law amounts are inputs so the composition is source-grounded without embedding an unencoded annual schedule". The commit subject is "Encode Missouri 2026 individual tax schedule" and the PR says "replace … with …"; no message, review, or comment anywhere calls the prior state wrong (PR #994 has zero reviews and was merged as a same-day draft-cycle PR). Post-fix values match the source table exactly, so nothing numeric was corrected — amount_mismatch is ruled out.

Two further meaning changes the reader did not cite, both secondary: every version gains `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` where the pre-fix versions were open-ended (143.011.5 requires annual bracket adjustment, so a timeless 2026 schedule would be wrong_period_or_effective_date — but pre-fix the values lived outside the module, so this mostly follows from the new parameter tables); and the caller input is renamed `mo_pit_pilot_supplied_taxable_income` → `mo_pit_pilot_individual_taxable_income` with a real `inputs:` block added (pre-fix the module declared no inputs at all; the supplied symbols existed only in test fixtures).

If the harness wants one label per commit and prefers the largest edit, unrepresented_clause is defensible at ~0.5; I put wrong_entity_or_scope slightly ahead because it needs no assumption about caller misuse and no contested reading of what the module claimed. Not mechanical and not not_a_defect under any reading: formulas, entities, versions and the output surface all changed.
